verdict.tagline: Rough initial menus clear the path to vast survival building.
for_you_if: you want deep survival crafting and building systems
you enjoy exploring massive procedural worlds by boat
not_for_you_if: you dislike heavy resource grinding and item transportation rules
you are frustrated by clunky combat and strict death penalties
you want polished interfaces right from the start

distortion_flags.sentence: Initial impressions are sharply divided before smoothing into strong approval among longer-term players.

cohorts.label: <2h refund window
cohorts.summary: Early players struggle with cluttered crafting menus and building interfaces.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the craft menu and building parts interface as cluttered, messy, and lacking further subdivisions beyond basic tabs.

citations.review_text:
This review is more aimed at casual players like me who are not familar with such games. The game feels like some's fading memory of a old Conan Exiles like game. I could personally vibe with the hazy visuals and rigid character design, but the onscreen text fonts, UI overlay lends to an overall very dated look. The tutorial guide as a raven is.. inspired? but the thought bubbles do not have a solid background. 

After that, the crafting menu seems like a mess. After the basic tabs dividing tools from building parts, there are no further subdivisions. So I have to look a cluttered boxed menu with 50 different parts ranging from roof parts to flooring, while 50 notifications pop up for the unlocking them. Then Overlay text that help with building itself consists entirely of small ugly floating text. It just feels messy, cheap and ugly.

It's surprising that despite the game's popularity the UI is left as is. Devs should really take a page out of Factorio's development and consider bring the UI to modern standards. Take inspiration, stay faithful to old games, except in terms of user-interface. 

Even though my playtime is short, the design choices I have seen so far do not lend me confidence and am likely to find further irritating elements as I continue. I wouldnt recommend this game if you are... sensitive? like me.

There are some bugs I noticed when I played this game 2 years ago. 1 issue is the hoe not leveling correctly, there is a mound that never gets flattened and I have to figure it out through Youtube and Reddit, which I shouldn't have to do. Some items like the pickaxe should be one of the 1st things to get when starting, why do I get an axe and a hammer to build, but no pickaxe? It makes no sense because there are rocks/boulders lying around which interfere with tools like the hoe. 

Other issues that aren't bug related are the tools, the building in this game is ok, not bad but not good, it's ok and it just does what it needs. But as someone who likes building in games, the line on the walls/half walls annoy me a bit, and the dirt phasing through the floor also annoys me, the stairs also seem to be restricted to only being put in 1 way and that's against the wall and up. I can't have it in the middle or in the corner, and I also can't make a balcony. 

This game is ok, I enjoyed it 2 years ago but now I just don't like it. There are more problems that occur, and the game hasn't really seemed to have progressed. It's the same game with nothing added to it, at least not in the beginning. Which is a bummer, the game should have a strong hold for beginners which then makes them want to finish the game, not have content at the end.

It could be just me, but building is a core mechanic in this game, which is why it's an issue for me. The game isn't terrible but something like that killed the vibe almost instantly.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the controls and combat feel clunky and difficult to use.

citations.review_text:
Given the game the controls are difficult to use. Switching views is stupid and there is NO information as to how to do various actions,
always doing the flying in thing is silly as well

The first few hours feel empty and devoid of diverse wildlife, you will kill the same boring things over and over, if you expect a polished, fast-paced modern survival game like I did coming from Conan Exiles, this may be a let down. 

Pros:  Immersive atmosphere and pretty decent weather/lighting systems. Cool concept. Cheaper/Lower priced compared to major survival games.

Cons: Clunky Combat and movement pacing feel incredibly sluggish and slow. Feels like I am playing someone's weekend project that never got finished. Frustrating building snap system is incredibly finicky. 

For a title in EA for 5 years this is disappointing and I just don't get the hype.
I will keep playing and may change my mind and review but as of 4 hours in, its very bland.
Whole thing just feels clunky, combat is incredibly unresponsive.

Pretty game, sure, but overburdened by clunky controls and RIDICULOUS enemy spawn rates. Greylings and Greydwarfs spawn SO much you will run into more within a full minute of the last swarm followed by Troll that will notice you in the far distance
My character got stuck in the ground 3 times and without a rake/shovel i had to restart a few more times
Hopefully the final update will actually fix that but im doubtful

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features a heavy and tedious resource grind.

citations.review_text: I only had a PS5 when this launched. i wanted to play it with my wife so bad. Now that we both have PCs its been an amazing game. if your the type that have a perfect duo or group and don't mind the "Minecraft" art style, this game is 1000% worth trying. The grind in the beginning can be tedious but figuring everything out and realizing your strength is one of the best parts. Taking out your first bear or troll gives a certain type of euphoria. 10/10 game.

Valheim is a deliberately slow paced experience that's supposed to feel mysterious and dangerous and it does a good job of that.

Unfortunately, the developers have mistaken "a slow pace" for "a tedious and punishing grind" that results in obviously unfair results, like putting 3 resources in and getting 1 back, when there were multiple steps before that, that they could've taken to reduce the output, if they felt that was necessary.

There's also a difference between keeping things vague and keeping them opaquely obscured. The first encourages exploration, the latter encourages looking things up online to skip the experimentation in an already punishing game.

Something I find that's clever, is that you need to stay scarce during the night. What's not clever, is just spamming monsters at the player to obviously punish them, instead of giving them the choice to do it anyway, with some resistance.

The game does not respect your time. That's the baseline issue here. It's not a "hardcore experience", it's just an otherwise enjoyable experience, hampered by a stubborn mind set.

Back to the drawing board boys, this ain't it.
One of the most mid games I have ever played. Cool concept, but theres too much grinding and not enough combat assiciated with the game.

dont get me wrong, this game is super fun and addicting, but it comes with many problems in my opinion. firstly, its annoying. its not hard, but some parts of the game are just so tedious and mindnumbing its hard to enjoy the experience. going to the black forest to mine copper or tin (UNREASONABLE AMOUNTS BTW) and then immediately being driven out by a troll or a bear is just so infuriating and annoying. running away for a minute and then coming back just to get aggroed by the same bear or troll. enemies in the black forest are so over-leveled for the average player going in, which leads me to my next point. this game is made for co-op, NOT singleplayer. i feel like the devs purposely made enemies so much harder than need be just for making playing with friends more fun. its very unfair for single players. as much as i dislike this part of the game, other parts are mostly great. i suppose maybe its because im in the copper age, which most players regard as the most tedious age, but its so annoying to keep playing. ill keep trying the game but if i have to run away from a bear or troll again for a solid two minutes then no way is the rest of the game fun.

claims.claim: Building mechanics require structural support and roofs to prevent collapse and weather damage to wood.

citations.review_text:
I have love hate relationships with this game. If not for my girlfriend, who likes game’s setting and wants to finish it but still share my opinion (as she later said, she was convincing herself that it’s good game just to not feel disappointment), I would drop it on 3th or 4th region without regrets. But let’s start with the positives:
-  This game really nailed viking esthetics, it’s even reflected in gameplay where you are expected to sail to some region build outpost and start developing your base with resources you find on site and starting extracting materials to move them to the main base when you gather enough. 
- Combat is another good* part of this game because it has elements such as blocking, parrying, dodging, combo of light attacks, special attacks that are weapon specific and variety of enemies to test your skills in combat. 
- Building also implemented in unique and interesting way where everything you build require support from sides and if support is removed the whole structure will collapse. Also wooden element require roof above them or rain will damage them until 50% hp applying visual affect on a component like it was abandoned and weather-beaten.
- Music at first seemed great, 1st region theme is very calming and really fits all location but after it I can’t really remember anything.
- Graphics can be called a plus of a game because it has its own style and I’ll leave it at that. I think it won’t be liked by everyone but I found it appealing.

And for the downsides I can address almost everything else because developers of Valheim seem to be obsessed with making game realistic and hyper complicated in every aspect. Right now game feels like set of interesting mechanics without clear vision what they trying to achieve. 
- To start inventory management is horrible, you got slot limits, count inside slot limits, weight limits, no additional slots for armor and trinkets which leads to situation where by the end of a game your 6 slots will be occup…

If you enjoy survival, exploration, building, and progression that feels rewarding rather than rushed, Valheim is one of the best games in its genre. Even years after its release, it remains highly recommended, especially if you play with friends or enjoy modding.

What Valheim does exceptionally well
🌍 Exploration (10/10)

The world is procedurally generated, so every seed feels different.

Each biome introduces:

New enemies
New resources
New mechanics
A new boss

Unlike many survival games, exploration is genuinely exciting because every new area matters.

🏠 Building (10/10)

Valheim has one of the best building systems in survival games.

Features include:

Structural integrity system
Snapping pieces
Huge creative freedom
Comfortable base mechanics
Terraforming

Players have recreated:

Viking castles
Japanese villages
Cities
Ships
Entire kingdoms

Mods make building even better.

⚔ Combat (8.5/10)

Combat focuses on:

Dodge rolls
Blocking
Perfect parries
Stamina management

Every enemy has strengths and weaknesses.

The combat isn't as deep as a Souls game, but it rewards preparation and timing more than button mashing.

⛵ Sailing (10/10)

One of Valheim's signature features.

You'll:

Build different ships
Navigate using the wind
Encounter sea serpents
Transport valuable metals
Go on long expeditions

Ocean journeys can become memorable adventures.

🎵 Atmosphere (10/10)

Valheim excels at creating mood.

Examples:

Peaceful mornings in the Meadows
Storms at sea
Misty forests
Snow-covered mountains
Eerie swamps

The soundtrack is subtle but highly effective.

📈 Progression (9.5/10)

Progression feels meaningful.

A typical cycle is:

Explore biome →
Collect resources →
Craft better gear →
Defeat boss →
Unlock next biome

Each upgrade noticeably changes what you're capable of.

Multiplayer (10/10)

Valheim shines with friends.

Builder

claims.claim: Resource gathering and transporting materials like iron require extensive back-and-forth travel and boat journeys.

citations.review_text:
The game is great. Maybe a little too much of a grind at a certein point of the game. It requires a lot of back and forth to gather resources. Like 70 iron to get a lvl 3 tool, which you have to melt for 21 minutes. And to get that iron you have to travel far away with a boat which can take up to 30-1hr to discover it,  discover cave fights to gather maybe around 100. a cave which may take up to 15 minutes to complete it. Go back with the boat for another 15~ ish minutes after you discover were it can be found, back to your home. 
The game runs great

Overall, I like this game, but it does a lot of things wrong, and I am only going to list those flaws. 

Playing it solo is a huge grind, and you have to deal with a lot, especially at night. Your stamina drops to zero very quickly, and you will be attacked by small enemies, bears, and trolls. Your items especially mining tools break easily, and your biggest enemy? Your inventory weight. You can't carry much, so you will have to constantly return to your base. Fun!

The world generation is random and it's the worst I've ever seen... I have never seen a reasonable generated map. I once played on a map that had almost no dungeons (all of them were five minutes away and far from each other). I generated another map where the first boss was close and there were multiple locations and dungeons, but the second boss was miles away at sea. I traveled by boat and died because, in order to reach it, I had to pass through a very high biome with flying enemies that one-shot you; you can't really do anything while you are on the boat.

Losing items at sea... oh boy... I went to complain about it, and people defended it to the death for some reason. 'It's realistic!' Yeah, it's 'realistic' to throw your items onto your ship and then realize there is no way to retrieve them, meaning they go straight into the sea, leaving you with no option of getting them back.

The biome enemy scaling is stupid. I get it you weren't meant to go there without the proper items but I beat trolls and bears, and you're telling me that a wolf does the same damage as a troll?! I went to see what the next biome was like, thinking I was ready, only to get one-shot by a wolf! Lol.

claims.claim: The game features a procedural world generation system that some find empty or repetitive.

citations.review_text:
Valheim is an empty world. Which is what you get with a procedurally generated world, it may be big, but it is empty in the sense that there really isn't a mission besides killing some bosses, sure you can build, but whats the point if the world is empty? 

The size of the world just serves to pad the game and it just feel like a waste of time and because it's generated everything always feel the same and areas just don't feel unique no matter if every generated world is different you''l always know what to expect.

Game is fun to play, but the graphic and generic auto-generated landscape and similar dungeons make it boring to play.  I'd rather playing something else with more hand crafted exciting places to explore.

cohorts.label: 100h+
cohorts.summary: Long-term players highlight addictive building systems alongside tedious gear retrieval, hostile biomes, and restricted metal transport.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that retrieving lost gear after dying in dangerous or remote biomes can be extremely tedious and difficult.

citations.review_text:
★★★★★ — 214.1 hrs on record — Would Sail the Ashlands Again

Honestly one of the best co-op experiences I've ever had. Valheim nails that Viking survival fantasy perfectly — from the first time you wash up on shore with nothing but a stone axe, to finally taking down Bonemass with a squad that's more focused on roasting each other in Discord than actually fighting the boss.

The building system is criminally addictive. What starts as "just a small base" turns into a full-blown fortress after hour 50, complete with someone's questionable tower design that "definitely won't collapse" (it collapsed). Exploring the biomes with friends — sailing into fog not knowing if you'll find loot or a Serpent about to end your voyage — never gets old.

But real talk, the actual magic of this game is playing it with friends. Half the fun isn't the boss fights or the loot, it's the chaos in voice chat — someone aggroing a troll by accident, someone else forgetting to eat and dying mid-raid, and the collective screaming when a Greydwarf sneaks up during base building. Valheim doesn't just give you a game, it gives you stories you'll be laughing about weeks later.

214 hours in and I'm still not tired of it. Simple graphics, deep gameplay, and a co-op experience that turns "let's just build a small house" into an all-night Discord call. Skål to that.

10/10 — best played with friends, a full pot of coffee, and zero regard for sleep schedule.

I love this game. I truly do. Everything in this game is perfect, exploration, soundtracks, enemies, weapons.
Every biome brings something new, something fresh, something new to grind and explore for which makes it really fun and addicting.

And then there's ashlands...

This biome is terrible. Everything tries to kill you in this biome. There ar dvergr from mistlands but they are too weak and there are so few of them to do anything(apart from the fact that they like to comit suicide in lava pools). Another annoying fact that none of the enemies fight each other, they all unite to kill you and trying to lose their agro is allmost impossible.

The worst part about this biome is if you die far away from your portal, trying to retrieve your loot is so tedious. I have spent over 1-2 hours to get my loot back because theres allways atleast one askvin or a ton of skeletons chasing me which you can't get rid of. Spending so much time doing the same thing gets so tedious and annoying you just want to quit and never play again.

Even after all this I still reccomend valheim from the bottom of my heart to everyone. This game is so good to not try it and the fact that 1.0 with Deep North being around the corner it brings hope that the new biome is going to be a lot better then the ashlands are.

(Lets hope that 1.0 will also bring some changes to ashlands)

I played this on normal without many modifiers, I suggest you change a lot of the core game rules:
The game has some balancing issues for sure, namely the mandatory Ashland zone that requires siege equipment to get to.  If you are a solo player that will require a lot of investment of resources and time.  If you are in a multiplayer server, it is still hard but more bearable.  I understand this is meant to be a multiplayer survival game however the pain of not having friends to support the base, venture out and collect resources (metal can not be teleported in base game settings) feels too long for the amount of materials you need to craft a single piece of armor or a weapon.  Using a massive amount of metal to make a sword that weighs about 90% of the blade should not be a thing, then double it to upgrade it to a reasonable level. The weapon itself may not even be effective at the monsters you are fighting such as skeletons, druagar, and trolls.  

Standard death makes you drop all your items at the tombstone, at least they won't float away.  Though you might wish it did float somewhere else because the gap in tiers needed to get to some locations are a bit too much and very painful to equip yourself to to retrieve the initial gear set.  Say I die in a hostile biome like the mountains, I have to climb the mountain or teleport up there with food in my belly to get all the equipment back.  And if I die with the previous tier of loot I had trying to get the first tombstone leads to a 2nd tombstone I have to retrieve.  It gets draining for sure.

Time needs to be allocated for growing and cooking food.  I am not really a farmer type but I like how different diets fit different playstyles but it feels more important than the armor you have.

The aesthetics are beautiful and picturesque at times, I don't experience much slow down on a 2080 turbo.  Though some of my friends complain when the game gets busy in the mist lands and some bosses.

This game has been in early ac…

Do I recommend this game?

If I could give a maybe I certainly would for this game.

I think it had a lot of really great decisions going into EA and each subsequent biome ruined the fun of the game a little more. They made some really bad choices like the mist being so obnoxious in mistlands, and the nonstop barrage of mobs in ashlands, raids on bases etc. Thankfully modders made the game better in every regard in fractions of the time Iron Gate takes to do literally ANYTHING.

Using a massive amount of metal to make a sword that weighs about 90% of the blade should not be a thing, then double it to upgrade it to a reasonable level. The weapon itself may not even be effective at the monsters you are fighting such as skeletons, druagar, and trolls.  

Standard death makes you drop all your items at the tombstone, at least they won't float away.  Though you might wish it did float somewhere else because the gap in tiers needed to get to some locations are a bit too much and very painful to equip yourself to to retrieve the initial gear set.  Say I die in a hostile biome like the mountains, I have to climb the mountain or teleport up there with food in my belly to get all the equipment back.  And if I die with the previous tier of loot I had trying to get the first tombstone leads to a 2nd tombstone I have to retrieve.  It gets draining for sure.

Time needs to be allocated for growing and cooking food.  I am not really a farmer type but I like how different diets fit different playstyles but it feels more important than the armor you have.

The aesthetics are beautiful and picturesque at times, I don't experience much slow down on a 2080 turbo.  Though some of my friends complain when the game gets busy in the mist lands and some bosses.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the building system as robust and addictive, allowing for the creation of elaborate structures while incorporating structural stability mechanics.

citations.review_text:
★★★★★ — 214.1 hrs on record — Would Sail the Ashlands Again

Honestly one of the best co-op experiences I've ever had. Valheim nails that Viking survival fantasy perfectly — from the first time you wash up on shore with nothing but a stone axe, to finally taking down Bonemass with a squad that's more focused on roasting each other in Discord than actually fighting the boss.

The building system is criminally addictive. What starts as "just a small base" turns into a full-blown fortress after hour 50, complete with someone's questionable tower design that "definitely won't collapse" (it collapsed). Exploring the biomes with friends — sailing into fog not knowing if you'll find loot or a Serpent about to end your voyage — never gets old.

But real talk, the actual magic of this game is playing it with friends. Half the fun isn't the boss fights or the loot, it's the chaos in voice chat — someone aggroing a troll by accident, someone else forgetting to eat and dying mid-raid, and the collective screaming when a Greydwarf sneaks up during base building. Valheim doesn't just give you a game, it gives you stories you'll be laughing about weeks later.

214 hours in and I'm still not tired of it. Simple graphics, deep gameplay, and a co-op experience that turns "let's just build a small house" into an all-night Discord call. Skål to that.

10/10 — best played with friends, a full pot of coffee, and zero regard for sleep schedule.

An Absolute Masterclass in Survival, Crafting, and Co-Op
Rating: ★★★★★ (5/5)
It is rare for an indie title to drop into the survival-crafting genre and instantly set a new high-water mark, but Valheim does precisely that. Blending Norse mythology, atmospheric world-building, and brilliant mechanics, it is easily one of the most compelling gaming experiences of the last decade.

One of Valheim’s biggest triumphs is how remarkably well it runs. In an era where modern releases routinely crush mid-tier rigs, Valheim manages to deliver stunning, painterly vistas with rich lighting and atmosphere while maintaining excellent performance on average PC hardware. You don't need a top-end graphics card to enjoy buttery-smooth framerates, making it incredibly accessible for groups of friends with varying PC setups.

Whether you want to drop into a quick session or run a persistent world for your group, Valheim makes seamless connectivity a priority. With robust private server support—including straightforward dedicated server setups—your community can build, explore, and progress at their own pace without worrying about tethering or host dependency.

If you enjoy base-building, prepare to be completely hooked. Valheim boasts some of the best building options in any game on the market. The structural integrity system forces you to think like an actual architect, balancing stability, airflow for smoke, and weather protection. From cozy coastal longhouses to sprawling mountain fortresses, the crafting system rewards creativity in a way few other games achieve.

While perfectly enjoyable solo, Valheim truly shines as a co-op game. Gathering resources, embarking on long naval voyages into uncharted waters, and tackling brutal boss fights alongside friends creates unforgettable gaming moments. The game’s immersion is top-notch—the howling winds during a thunderstorm, the dynamic ocean swells, and the quiet beauty of the Meadows make the world feel alive and unforgiving.

Progression …

Valheim is a good, cozy survival game overall that captures a uniquely warm atmosphere. Its beloved low-poly, retro visual style paired with stunning dynamic lighting and weather effects creates a charming aesthetic that players fall in love with instantly.

The building capabilities are remarkably detailed, forcing you to account for structural stability and smoke ventilation. However, the system is somewhat limited by a lack of geometric shapes, which can restrain your creativity when trying to build more intricate vanilla structures.

The progression system is fine and satisfying, taking you smoothly from one biome to the next as defeating regional bosses unlocks the tools and metals needed for your next leap in technology.

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that the development and update pace has been slow during early access.

citations.review_text:
The graphics, mood, vibes, absolutely spectacular. I had a great time with this game with friends and family.

On the other hand, the update pace, is an absolute insult. Modders have done 100x more than the team ever has. I am asking for ONE, I repeat, ONE, substantial update. You don't need to support the game for years. It's just I've never seen a single actual satisfying content release. The team members seem to be apathetic about delivering substantial updates, I have watched their interviews and conference talks. 

This game and 7DTD and Zomboid have put serious PTSD in buying open-world survival crafting games in Early Access for me, because I see promise in them and when I purchased them, while I am indeed enjoying the game, I purchased them on the premise that I believed there would be at least ONE major update within 2 years of their initial release. Most of these games I've been waiting longer than 5 years now.

Shoutout to the modding community for making this game what it is today.

When the game first dropped in alpha, it was actually really fun and had a ton of potential. My friends and I played it for a solid 2-3 play throughs in the last few years and had a blast. We were excited to see where the devs would take it.

Fast forward five years, and the official updates have been extremely underwhelming, Valheim is a good game that got carried by an incredible modding community, but the development pace has been painfully slow for a game that exploded as hard as it did.

Thankfully, the modding community stepped up and basically finished the game for them years ago. The mods added the depth, replayability, and content that kept the game alive.

The content they are finishing up in this full release has already been finished years ago with mods. It mostly just means the game is probably going to be broken for a few weeks or months while modders have to update everything again.

Do I recommend this game?

If I could give a maybe I certainly would for this game.

I think it had a lot of really great decisions going into EA and each subsequent biome ruined the fun of the game a little more. They made some really bad choices like the mist being so obnoxious in mistlands, and the nonstop barrage of mobs in ashlands, raids on bases etc. Thankfully modders made the game better in every regard in fractions of the time Iron Gate takes to do literally ANYTHING. 

It certainly gave me a few hours of entertainment for the money I spent but I will never buy another EA from these slow ass developers again. 5+ years to release 3 major updates.
